source_text: Primus igitur eius liber, qui ante hunc solus est editus, novos nos esse haereticos criminatur [n9] ; quia repugnemus opinioni, quae dealbati instar sepulcri, quod secundum Evangelii sententiam, mundo extrinsecus colore vestitum, spurcitia est et iniquitate confertum [n10] , sub laude Baptismatis eructat Manichaeorum sordes ac naturale peccatum, ut Ecclesiae catholicae pura hactenus Sacramenta contaminet.
pass_a_gloss: His first book therefore, which alone was published before this, accuses us of being new heretics; because we fight against an opinion which, like a whitewashed tomb, which according to the Gospel's sentence, clothed outwardly with a clean color, is packed with filth and iniquity, under praise of Baptism belches the filths of the Manichaeans and natural sin, so as to contaminate the Sacraments of the catholic Church, pure until now.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: His first book, then, the only one published before this, accuses us of being new heretics (Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 1.1). The reason is that we oppose an opinion which, like the whitewashed tomb of the Gospel, is covered outwardly with a clean surface but packed with filth and wickedness within (Matthew 23:27). Under the guise of praising baptism, it belches out the filth of the Manichaeans and sin inherent in nature, contaminating the catholic Church's sacraments, which until now have been pure.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
